solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fitted pegs?

parts.note: pegs is slang for teeth, and fitted ones are dentures put in by a dentist rather than grown

explanation.surface: A joiner or camper has just fixed some pegs into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are artificial teeth, playfully called pegs, which a dentist fits into the mouth.

clue.text: Fixed abode

definitions.meaning: a ... rate or fee is a fixed one
a home, such as an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: Flat means fixed, as in a flat fee, and is also a British word for an apartment, a dwelling.

clue.text: Look — is this a wind-up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to wind in a line is to reel it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sly glance is meant as a tease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind-up' reads as British slang for a tease, but split it: wind gives REEL and 'up' turns it over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive or unpleasant look at someone.

clue.text: Make a mistake with mission

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone blunders while on an assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip taken to do a task, a small mission.

clue.text: Miracle taxman OK to fiddle!

indicators.note: to fiddle is to tamper with or cook the books, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a tax inspector approves of cheating, worth a shriek!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the closing ! is the very symbol described, and the shock it expresses fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark ! signals surprise, as at a taxman approving fraud, so the clue both shows and builds it.

clue.text: Chase it for game? It's hard to miss for cunning cheetah!

indicators.note: cunning suggests craft and contrivance, so the remaining letters are artfully rearranged
missing means left out, so one letter drops out of the cat's name

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A predator is told it will struggle to catch the game it chases.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from CHEETAH to leave CEETAH, which 'cunning' rearranges. Chase the Ace is an old card game, so the answer fills the gap in 'Chase it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chase the Ace is a traditional card game, so these two words complete the game's name in place of it.

clue.text: His victim was The Third Man

definitions.text: His victim was The Third Man

parts.words: His victim was The Third Man
parts.note: the Bible's first family runs Adam, then Cain, then the younger brother Cain murdered, so the victim was the third man ever

explanation.surface: A reference to the Orson Welles film noir about a mysterious murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man looks like the 1949 film; it means the third human being. The blog reports the clue was meant to start 'This victim', and 'His' refers to Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel, son of Adam, was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, making him the first murder victim and the third man.

clue.text: Supermarket delivery somewhat late?

parts.note: a wholemeal loaf is something a supermarket delivers, and in Cockney rhyming slang that loaf stands for dead, a sense of late

explanation.surface: A grocery order turns up behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it: brown bread rhymes with dead, and the late are the deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown bread is a supermarket staple and also rhyming slang for dead, which is what late means of a person.

clue.text: Seaside tour's final location? I really didn't want to go there

definitions.meaning: the final stop on a tour of coastal holiday towns

definitions.text: I really didn't want to go there
definitions.meaning: a choice taken only when everything else has failed

explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is a final option used reluctantly, and punningly the final seaside town visited.

clue.text: Perhaps between 3 and 7 years old represented thus…

definitions.text: Perhaps between 3 and 7 years old represented thus…

parts.words: Perhaps between 3 and 7 years old represented thus…
parts.note: the enumeration (3-7) written in brackets is a range of years, which is exactly what this kind of grouping shows

explanation.surface: A description of children aged three to seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to other clues; they are the age range, and the enumeration (3-7) shows them in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: An age bracket is a range of ages grouped together, such as three to seven years.

clue.text: Like the onset of WW2 intelligence

definitions.meaning: America stayed out until Pearl Harbor in 1941

explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for practical intelligence or common sense, and split in two it describes a war without the United States.

clue.text: Court invited into Frenchman's second home

indicators.note: being invited into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A suitor is asked into a French man's holiday flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small secondary residence, typically a city flat kept for occasional stays.

clue.text: Solved buying an admission ticket? —— —-, he didn't charge much!

definitions.text: buying an admission ticket? —— —-, he didn't charge much!
definitions.meaning: split the answer as 6 and 4 letters, ..., to fill the gap: a ticket tout who sold cheaply

explanation.definitionFit: Thought out means worked out carefully, and split as though tout it completes the remark about a cheap ticket seller.

clue.text: One age for Man in dream

parts.note: taken as written
a fancy is a daydream or whim

explanation.surface: A single era in which humankind lived in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' recalls Shakespeare's seven ages of man, the first being the infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the first of the ages of man, the earliest stage of life.

clue.text: Tend to go up or down

definitions.meaning: to have a leaning towards something
to slope, as a hill does

explanation.definitionFit: Incline means to tend towards something and also to slope upwards or downwards.

clue.text: A farm employee, I am randy — dreadfully!

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A farmhand confesses to being lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is a link: the farm worker speaks, and only 'am randy' is rearranged. Randy is British slang for lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman is a labourer who works in a farmyard, so he is a farm worker.

clue.text: Where one might find 5 under control

definitions.meaning: a card held is in the player's grasp, as the ace from 5 down might be

explanation.definitionFit: In hand means under control, and an ace in one's hand is where a card player would hold it.

clue.text: Source of shady income for only the middle-class?

indicators.note: keeping only the middle means the first and last letters are dropped from the group

parts.note: a class is a group of learners

explanation.surface: A question whether a dodgy money-maker benefits only the middle classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-class' looks like one social idea; split it: class gives LEARNERS and 'only the middle' trims its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nice little earner is a profitable, often dubious, money-making scheme.

clue.text: Two flags unfairly applied to some but not others

definitions.meaning: a pair of banners, standards being flags

definitions.text: unfairly applied to some but not others

explanation.definitionFit: Double standards are principles applied inconsistently, and literally a pair of flags.

clue.text: Exotic island loses time installing name for sesame product

indicators.note: losing means one letter goes, replaced by another
installing means a new letter is put in where the old one went

parts.note: Tahiti is a South Pacific island

explanation.surface: A tropical island swaps something over to make a sesame paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses' takes out the second T of TAHITI and 'installing' puts N in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds, used in hummus.

clue.text: Area of Greece taken in with a camera

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the letters run inside these words

explanation.surface: A Greek region photographed by a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, home of Odysseus.

clue.text: Some might say extravagant charity fair

indicators.note: what some people say signals a word spoken that sounds like the answer

parts.note: something extravagant or outlandish is bizarre

explanation.surface: Some people call a charity sale over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some might say' hedges because the two words sound alike only in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a fundraising sale of goods, as held by a church or charity.

clue.text: Northern Ireland party about to enforce exile

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A political party in Ulster is set to impose banishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political beside Northern Ireland but it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to force them into exile.

clue.text: Vulgar one ain't from a public school!

indicators.note: vulgar suggests something rough and corrupted, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crude person saying ain't cannot have been to a posh school!
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an elite fee-paying school; Eton is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil or former pupil of Eton College, the British public school.

clue.text: Fleece one of the four men cornered

definitions.text: one of the four men cornered
definitions.meaning: a chess piece starting in a corner square, of which there are four

explanation.definitionFit: Rook means to swindle, and the rook is the chess piece that begins in each corner of the board.

clue.text: I'm disturbed by some dismissals from security

definitions.meaning: in cricket a small crosspiece on the stumps is knocked off when a batsman is bowled or stumped
money paid to free an accused person pending trial

explanation.definitionFit: Bail is money given as security for release, and the bails in cricket fall when a batsman is bowled.

clue.text: Child drops from second slide

indicators.note: in a down entry, dropping from means coming below, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster falls off a playground slide in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slide uncontrollably, as a car does on ice.

clue.text: Seeing wild animals here from a distance, I power across island

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so one piece spans the others

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
afar means from far away

explanation.surface: A traveller views the wildlife from far off while flying an aircraft over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari park is an enclosure where visitors drive among wild animals.

clue.text: Food? English and Irish poets both neglecting starters

indicators.note: neglecting starters means the first letters are dropped, and both poets give the same remainder

parts.note: Keats was an English poet and Yeats an Irish one; either serves

explanation.surface: A question whether poets from two nations skip the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of KEATS or of YEATS and the same four letters remain. 'Starters' hints at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, as in tasty eats.

clue.text: Flash bloke, knave held at resort

parts.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A showy man is detained at a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a seaside town; read it as re-sort, giving THELAD from HELD AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack the lad is a brash, cocky young man, British slang for a flash bloke.
